items.source: Merriam-Webster, "OK" (etymology: abbreviation of "oll korrect", a facetious spelling of "all correct"; first known use 1839); Online Etymology Dictionary, "OK" (etymonline.com/word/OK: 1839, Boston newspaper slang, as traced by the linguist Allen Walker Read).

model_answer.id: "OK" lahir sebagai lelucon. Pada 1839, sebuah koran di Boston menulis "O.K." untuk "oll korrect", salah eja yang disengaja dari "all correct" (semua beres). Kini "OK" dipakai di seluruh dunia.
model_answer.en: "OK" started as a joke. In 1839 a Boston newspaper wrote "O.K." for "oll korrect", a playful misspelling of "all correct". Now people say it all over the world.

items.source: Online Etymology Dictionary, "million" (etymonline.com/word/million: from Old French million, from Italian millione (now milione), literally "a great thousand", from mille "thousand"); Merriam-Webster, "million" (etymology).

model_answer.id: Kata "million" masuk ke bahasa Inggris lewat bahasa Prancis dari kata Italia lama millione, kira-kira "seribu yang besar": seribu kali seribu. Jadi, one million rupiah = Rp1.000.000.
model_answer.en: "Million" came into English through French from the old Italian millione, roughly "a great thousand": a thousand thousands. So one million rupiah is Rp1,000,000.
